resources.string: The built-in shell isn\'t running, and neither is Shizuku. Set up the built-in shell above, or start Shizuku, then come back.

Applied each time this game starts from Games: its controller, keys and on-screen controls go into Dolphin then, with nothing to set in Dolphin. Opened from Dolphin itself, a game plays with the controls of the last game started from Games. Invisible on-screen controls are needed for sticks and keys placed on the screen.
Invisible (for sticks and keys placed on them)
Tap a button to give it a key, alone or with a modifier. Buttons with this game\'s own key are outlined, and a key given here presses only that button.
Give the %1$s\'s buttons and movements keys of this game\'s own, such as a wheelie button. Kept as a Dolphin profile for this game.
Saved. Dolphin uses it from the next time this game starts from Games.
This game plays with the controls set here, even if a profile was chosen for it in Dolphin. Off: a profile chosen in Dolphin is kept.
Move the phone as the Wii Remote
Tilting, turning and shaking the phone moves the Wii Remote, from the phone\'s own motion sensors. The keys for tilt, swing and shake still work too.
The phone no longer moves the Wii Remote in this game
The phone moves the Wii Remote in this game
Cemu shows the Wii U GamePad\'s screen from its in-game menu (Show pad), placed where its settings say (General). It keeps both in its private settings, so Flux Gaming can\'t set them per game.
Written into NooDS\'s settings now. NooDS reads them when it opens, for every game: it has no settings per game. Screen is set to suit it.
%1$s keeps its screen layout in its own private settings, which Flux Gaming can\'t reach: set it in %1$s\'s settings or in-game menu.

Written into %1$s\'s settings as a game starts from Games (an app\'s also now, for games started in %1$s itself). Screen is set to suit it: Portrait for one above the other, Landscape for the rest. The trackpad\'s bottom-screen area follows it. Catch: if you\'ve used Swap Screens in %1$s, the screens come out the other way round, so swap them back there.
Set up gaming mode for it: controller, screen and sticks.
Found among your games. Set up its controller, screen and sticks now, or play it with %1$s\'s settings.
This game isn\'t on the phone any more
Change which key is which button here alone, on top of Keyboard controls. Works in any emulator or launcher gaming mode sends buttons to.
Keys changed here apply only while this plays, on top of Keyboard controls. Each key shows its button, alone or with the modifier chosen here held. Tap a key to change it.
A part of it that plays its games under another name, like a launcher\'s player.
In Azahar\'s Settings, Graphics: Graphics API %1$s, Internal resolution 1×, Disk shader cache on, Asynchronous shader compilation on. Lighter games can take 2×.
What to change in its own settings for smooth play
In Eden\'s Settings, Graphics: Resolution 0.75× (1× for lighter games), Accuracy Normal, Asynchronous shaders on, Disk shader cache on.

In Eden\'s Settings, Graphics: Resolution 0.5×, Accuracy Normal, Asynchronous shaders on, Disk shader cache on. This phone\'s Mali GPU runs fewer Switch games than Adreno phones do: check reports for a game first.
In the game\'s own settings: graphics quality Medium or Low, a 60 fps limit only if it stays steady (else 30), and render scale or resolution below 100% if it offers one.

In %1$s, the game\'s (or its container\'s) settings: Graphics driver %2$s, DXVK for DirectX 9 to 11 games (WineD3D if one won\'t start), VKD3D for DirectX 12, Screen size 1280×720, Box64 preset Performance.
Use a picture from the phone
Covers show in the Games app and Moonlight; square artwork on shortcuts and in settings.
No artwork found online. Try searching for its title above.
Press Back again to leave the game
Keyboard controls, and what the keyboard can play
Its settings and art go. A game found again later comes back as new.

The keyboard isn\'t a controller: it has no real sticks, and its keys and the volume keys do all the work, so gaming mode suits games that play on buttons. Your mileage may vary. For the best experience, use a controller over Bluetooth or USB, ideally one made for a phone held upright or one with a phone clip.
A folder you already use in a launcher or emulator.
Creates Download/Flux Keyboard/Games with a folder for each launcher and emulator. ES-DE\'s ROMs folder is read too.

Created in Download/Flux Keyboard/Games. For GameNative, go to Settings > Interface > Frontend Sync and choose the GameNative folder. For the official GameHub, set its Export for frontend to the GameHub folder.
The official GameHub can only be opened, not told which game to start. Install GameHub Lite alongside it: the games the official GameHub exports then start straight away in GameHub Lite.

GameHub Lite has no Export for frontend. Install the official GameHub alongside it and set its Export for frontend to the GameHub folder in Download/Flux Keyboard/Games: its games are then listed here and start in GameHub Lite.
GameNative\'s games only take sticks from a real controller or its on-screen controller, so your keys move the on-screen sticks (kept invisible).

In GameNative, once per game:
1. Start the game and open its menu (Back).
2. Turn on the On-screen Controller, with its default layout.
3. Set Control Opacity to 0.

Your keys then move its sticks (W A Z D, and Alt with I J M L). To press its buttons, place keys on them from the gaming mode notification.

To play with the phone upright, turn on Portrait Mode in the game's settings, General.
In the app list, moved through with keys, in the quick launcher and on the home screen
A shortcut that starts it with these settings.
Your home screen doesn\'t accept shortcuts.
From GameNative, GameHub or your game folders, each with a home screen shortcut, or a game you added to a launcher or emulator yourself.
No games found. Add a game to the home screen from its launcher, or add the launcher itself.
Your keys play as a controller (see Keyboard controls). For touch-only games, place keys on its buttons from the gaming mode notification.
Your keys play as a controller in %1$s (see Keyboard controls). Keys you place on screen tap there instead.

Left stick: W A Z D (S clicks it)
D-pad: right Shift + W A Z D
Right stick: left Shift + I J M L, or SYM + W A Z D (K clicks it, SYM + S too)
Face buttons: I (Y), J (X), M (A), L (B)
Bumpers: Q and E
Triggers: Volume Down (left) and Volume Up (right) (Alt + Volume: pressed all the way without the click, for a GameCube controller)
Start: Space
Select: Shift + Space
Xbox / Home: Alt + Space
Volume: SYM + Volume Up or Down

Keys placed on a game's screen tap there instead.
None of the launchers or emulators Flux Gaming can start games in is installed (GameNative, GameHub, GameHub Lite, Dolphin, PPSSPP, Azahar, Eden).
Uses %1$s\'s settings. Turn this on if this game needs different ones.
This game has its own trackpad, screen and stick settings.
The phone\'s own game mode, and Shell access
Drag each key onto the game\'s button, and each circle onto its stick. Add a key, then press it or pick it.
Allow Flux Gaming to display over other apps, then try again.
The stream\'s screen is a different shape from the one its keys were placed on, so they may miss the game\'s buttons. Tap to place them for the stream (kept apart from the phone\'s).
How far the pointer moves when you slide your finger. It moves on from where it is, not to where you touch.
Pick a key below, or press it.
Shows your games in the quick launcher, opening them the same way as their home screen shortcuts.
Puts everything Flux Gaming changed in %1$s (controls, graphics, per-game controllers) back how it was. Changes made by older versions of Flux Gaming can\'t be undone.
Everything set there from here, put back as it was.
%1$s\'s settings are back to how they were before Flux Gaming changed them.
When kept upright, the game renders at this height and is scaled up to fill the screen. Lower runs smoother.
The game rotates the screen as it likes. In GameNative, turn on Portrait mode in the game\'s settings (General) to play upright.
The game gets a landscape screen while you hold the phone upright, and the screen doesn\'t turn. Best for most games. It\'s slightly shorter, to stay clear of the camera.
The game gets the whole upright screen, whatever it asks for. For DS and 3DS emulators (their two screens one above the other), phone games made for portrait, and vertical arcade games.
The last app a game ran in (%1$s) has no profile. Some launchers run games in a separate app: add it to the launcher\'s profile so gaming mode stays on during play.

%1$s can\'t load controls from a file. In its Settings, under Input (Controls), bind each button by pressing its key when asked:
%2$s
The keyboard\'s controls written into %1$s\'s own controller settings, its graphics too where they can be.

%1$s\'s controls now follow Flux Gaming\'s keyboard controls (see Keyboard controls).\n\nDolphin: GameCube controller 1 (L and R on the volume keys, Z on E) and Wii Remote 1 with Nunchuk are set, the pointer following the trackpad\'s right half. PPSSPP: its controls are set for every game.
Couldn\'t find %1$s\'s settings. Open it once, then try again.
Add games, game folders, GameHub and Xbox Cloud Gaming
Nintendo\'s layout: M presses B, L presses A, I presses X and J presses Y, so each key presses the button in its place. On by default for Nintendo emulators.
In games with a profile, your keys play as a controller or tap the game\'s on-screen buttons.
If both sticks won\'t move at once: tap, then move a finger on each half of the trackpad for %1$d seconds. Saved to Download/Flux Keyboard/trackpad-test.txt so you can share it.
Most fingers seen at once: %1$d (%2$s).\n\nSaved to Download/Flux Keyboard/trackpad-test.txt.
Recording… move two fingers on the trackpad
Graphics: %1$s, native resolution, shaders built in the background (things may appear a moment late instead of stuttering), dual core on, VSync off. Raise the resolution in Dolphin for lighter games.
Graphics: %1$s, 2× resolution, shaders built in the background, dual core on, VSync off.
Graphics: %1$s, 2× PSP resolution, no frame skipping, hardware transform and skinning on.
Graphics: %1$s, 3× PSP resolution, no frame skipping, hardware transform and skinning on.
Play Xbox Cloud Gaming in Flux Gaming\'s own player (the Xbox apps don\'t stream on phones). Pick a game from the catalogue: it gets its own settings and opens straight into the game.
Adds it to the Games app and Moonlight\'s list without playing it. Games you play are added by themselves.
In your games: in the Games app and Moonlight.
Couldn\'t load the catalogue. Check the phone is online and offline mode is off.
Plays in Flux Gaming\'s own player. Sign in once, then your keys work as a controller in every game.
The XCloud catalogue lists only the cloud games your plan includes, from Microsoft\'s own Game Pass lists.
Sign in to Xbox in Flux Gaming\'s player. Once signed in, every cloud game plays.
Cloud games won\'t play until you sign in again.
Signed in to Xbox in Flux Gaming\'s player.
Each button shows the keys that press it. Tap a button to pick its key, alone or with a modifier: the keys that pressed it before then press nothing.
Each key shows the button it is, alone or with the modifier chosen here held. Tap a key to change it.
Dolphin reads the keys from its own settings: changes here are written there the next time a Dolphin game starts from Games or Gaming settings opens.

Changed keys are outlined. For games played only by touch, keys can also be placed on the game\'s screen: Place keys on screen, in gaming mode\'s notification while the game is open. A placed key taps there instead.
Nothing (goes to the game as it is)
Press the key on the keyboard (with a modifier held if you like), or tap it below.
Every key back to the layout\'s button
See and change which keys are which buttons
Keys on it now (tap one to take it off):
Controller keys in the Games app

Move through the Games app with the same keys as in games: W A Z D to move, M to open, J for a game\'s settings, L to go back, Q or E to switch between games and launchers, Space for gaming settings. A controller works too.
No games yet. Add one with Add a game, or create the game folders in Gaming settings.
Your games and their apps are set up there: long-press a tile.
Add every game to the home screen
A home screen shortcut with its art for each game with a profile. The home screen asks for each one.
Unihertz\'s Game Mode can take over as the home screen alongside gaming mode. Turn it off here.
Gaming mode reads your keys through it. If Android calls it a restricted setting, allow restricted settings in the app\'s info first.
Gaming mode\'s notification places keys on the screen and switches profiles.
Placing keys on a game\'s own buttons draws over the game.
Gaming mode sends keys and touches to games through it.
Streaming is on. Streamed: %1$s is turned on and Moonlight opens there, straight into the game.

Gaming mode reads the keys before the game does, so in a game the keyboard plays it, and sees which app’s screen is in front to pick its profile. It never reads what’s on the screen, and does nothing while gaming mode is off.
Game art from SteamGridDB, the Libretro thumbnails and the game launchers themselves. Xbox Cloud Gaming plays in Flux Gaming’s own player, on xbox.com.
